Calibrate it: with the Space on the glasses, tap Check delay. A thin line appears fixed in the room. Turn your head gently left and right and move the slider until the line stays put, then tap Save run. Move the slider to one end before each run. Three runs within 1 ms of each other set the delay for these glasses.
Calibrated: the glasses\' sensor reads roll %1$.2f, pitch %2$.2f degrees when the picture is level.
Not calibrated: the sensor is taken as level with the picture.

Once per pair of glasses: with the Space on the glasses, tap Check level. A green line appears across the middle of the view. Look at a level edge at eye height (the horizon, a far shelf or window frame), tilt your head until the line lies on it, hold still, then tap Save level. The sensor may read up to 50 degrees of pitch (the Aura\'s sits about 14.5 degrees tilted, a One Pro more, a One Pro+ about 40) and 10 of roll.

On in 3D since 0.5.25, with the 60 Hz row model: if the picture tilts during head turns in 3D, turn it off there. Late warp in 3D draws the Space early and turns it by the newest head pose just before each frame is due, so a slow frame no longer jumps.

Record motion for 20 seconds saves what your glasses\' motion sensor sends over USB, so support for them can be added. With the Space on the glasses, tap Calibrate and pinch on each of the five dots it shows, pointing at each one. It corrects the glasses camera\'s angle and field of view. The Space offers it once by itself the first time it sees your hands; an open palm skips it.

Outside the Space, hands and the trackpad reach the glasses through an accessibility service. It is the only way Android lets an ordinary app act on other apps\' windows. It comes with the Pocket XR add-on, a second small app, because Google blocks installing apps with one in some countries. It:

- draws the cursor, hints and the dock on the glasses display
- reads where app windows are on the glasses (position, size and title only), and the labels of DeX's title bar buttons there, to find its full screen button
- performs taps and drags on the glasses display, which is how windows are clicked, moved (drag on the DeX title bar) and resized (drag on a corner)
